CONTEXT.content: Vague requirements kill projects. A vertical slice is a thin, end-to-end feature that delivers user value. Good planning decomposes big features into slices with clear acceptance criteria.
CONTEXT.analogy: Building a house floor-by-floor (horizontal) means no one can live in it until it's done. Building room-by-room (vertical) means each room is usable as you go.
CONTEXT.productionNote: Teams that plan in layers ship nothing for months. Teams that plan in slices ship value every week.
hints: Is 'build the database' a vertical slice? Why or why not?

DECIDE.optionA: Plan by layer: database schema → API → UI, building each completely before moving on.
DECIDE.optionB: Plan by vertical slice: thinnest end-to-end feature first, then expand.

tradeoffs.A: Clean architecture early; no user value until all layers done.
tradeoffs.B: User value fast; may need refactoring as slices expand.

hints: For a URL shortener, what's the thinnest slice that a user would pay for?

BUILD.goal: Write a decomposition plan for adding 'link analytics' to your URL shortener: 3 vertical slices with acceptance criteria each.

tracks.general: Produce a written plan (markdown or text) — no code required for this module.

acceptance: Each slice has: goal, scope boundaries, dependencies, acceptance criteria
hints: Acceptance criteria must be testable — not 'works well'.

criteria: Another engineer could implement Slice 1 from your plan alone
hints: Hand your plan to someone (or imagine you are) — what's ambiguous?

BREAK.scenario: Mid-build, the PM adds: 'Analytics must also track geographic location of clicks.'
BREAK.symptoms: Your Slice 2 is half-built. The new requirement affects Slice 1's data model.
hints: Which slice does this change affect?
Do you restart, adapt, or add a new slice?

FIX.goal: Revise your plan to absorb the new requirement without throwing away completed work.
hints: Good plans have explicit scope boundaries — you should know exactly what's affected.
Adaptation speed matters more than perfect plans.

decisionCallbacks.A: Layer planning made the scope change expensive — you'd need to redo the data model layer.
decisionCallbacks.B: Vertical slices let you add geo-tracking as a new thin slice without rewriting Slice 1.
